title: Anomalous post-failover metering offsets caused by sticky retry header propagation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported unexplained token usage spikes immediately following a cross-region failover which correlated with retries from edge proxies. Incidents affected Hosted and Dedicated tenants (two large customers on Dedicated) and one Private deployment where a local proxy preserved a retry header across failover.
root_cause_summary: During region failover and request rerouting we observed a mismatch between retry id propagation and the in-memory idempotency/deduplication index used by the accounting layer. Clients and proxies were setting a sticky retry header (Idempotency-Key / X-Client-Retry-Id) to enable safe retries. When a request was replayed to a different runtime pool after failover the deduplication metadata had been evicted or not migrated, so the runtime treated the replayed request as new. Additionally, streaming token accounting paths were instrumented differently from standard request accounting: the streaming path incremented per-chunk token counts before consulting dedup logic, producing half-counts and later full-count duplication in ledger aggregation. The combination produced durable, reproducible double-counts and partial token fragments on aggregated rollups across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a client/proxy to add a stable Idempotency-Key header on retries.
2) Start a long streaming generation on a tenant pinned to region A.
3) Simulate region failover by draining and re-routing traffic to region B (test harness uses traffic-muxer-v2).
4) Retry the client request while the dedup index is cold on region B.
5) Observe doubled token counts in per-request logs and in the central metering pipeline within 30-90s.
6) Compare streaming chunk accounting vs non-streaming accounting to see inconsistent dedup checks.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to runtime-1.21: (a) ensure idempotency-key is canonicalized and forwarded to the accounting proxy; (b) add a fast-path lookup in the streaming accounting flow to consult the persistent dedup store before emitting token increments; (c) increase dedup TTL for active sessions to 120s during failover windows. Deployed to Hosted and Dedicated within 2 hours of escalation and staged to Private customers with an opt-in patch. Immediate customer credits issued for identified overcharges (see backfill_actions).
rollback_plan: Hotfix is a safe, additive check. If regressions observed revert streaming fast-path to previous behavior and re-open non-blocking patch revert PR. Coordinate with on-call infra to toggle feature-flag 'dedup-precheck-stream' per-cluster.
backfill_actions: 1) Run reconciliation job 'recon/dedup-replay-202502' to detect duplicate request IDs and sum duplicate token deltas.
2) For affected tenants produce ledger adjustments as preliminary credit notes and notify billing team.
3) Provide CSV per-customer with request-ids, timestamps, delta tokens and proposed credit amounts.
4) Schedule a follow-up job to regularly scan for stale dedup TTLs until dedup migrations complete.

notes: Long-term solution options: (A) persist dedup index into strongly-consistent store with cross-region replication (higher cost), (B) embed dedup metadata in client-signed tokens for deterministic dedup across clusters (requires client changes), (C) unify streaming and non-streaming accounting codepaths to a single dedup-first model. Engineering recommends (C) + short-term (A) for high-risk tenants.
